title: Causal Language Modeling
description: Train decoder-only Transformers to predict the next token and generate text autoregressively.
content:
**Causal language modeling** trains a model on one simple objective: given the previous tokens, predict the next one. Because attention is **causal (masked)** - each position may attend only to itself and the past - the trained model can generate text **autoregressively**: produce one token, append it, repeat until the EOS token.

**GPT** is the canonical **decoder-only** Transformer implementing this recipe. It stacks Transformer decoder blocks with masked multi-head self-attention, position-wise feed-forward networks, residuals and layer normalization; there is no encoder and no cross-attention. Pretraining on massive corpora of raw text yields general language competence, and the same next-token machinery then serves tasks as varied as dialogue, summarization and code generation - often steered purely through the prompt.

> Properties of the decoder-only stack:
> • Objective: P(next token | previous tokens) - exactly what inference does
> • Generation is autoregressive, one token at a time, stopped by the EOS token
> • No lookahead: the training conditions match the inference conditions

The elegance of causal LM is this alignment: the model is trained to do precisely what it will be asked to do at generation time.
